analysis.evidence: In זֶה סֵפֶר תּוֹלְדֹת אָדָם, “This is the record of Adam’s generations,” זֶה stands as the subject of a verbless clause. The predicate סֵפֶר תּוֹלְדֹת אָדָם identifies the record to which it points.
analysis.morphology: Independent masculine singular demonstrative pronoun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Introduces the written record that follows.

analysis.evidence: זֶה סֵפֶר תּוֹלְדֹת אָדָם means “This is the written record of Adam’s generations.” The construct chain identifies the contents of the record as Adam’s genealogy.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In זֶה סֵפֶר תּוֹלְדֹת אָדָם, the construct noun תּוֹלְדֹת takes אָדָם as its complement. The phrase introduces the written account of Adam’s descendants.
analysis.sense: generations, the account of what came from someone

analysis.evidence: In סֵפֶר תּוֹלְדֹת אָדָם, “the book of the generations of Adam,” אָדָם completes the construct chain and names the ancestor. The genealogy then gives Adam’s age at the birth of Seth (Genesis 5:3).
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun in the absolute state, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Adam, the ancestor whose genealogy follows

analysis.evidence: בְּיוֹם governs the infinitive construct בְּרֹא. The phrase בְּיוֹם בְּרֹא אֱלֹהִים אָדָם means “when God created humankind” and gives the time of עָשָׂה אֹתוֹ, “he made him.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with the prefixed preposition בְּ.
analysis.sense: the time when; on the day that

analysis.evidence: בְּיוֹם בְּרֹא אֱלֹהִים אָדָם means “when God created humankind.” אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the infinitive and אָדָם its object. The following clause describes the same act as making humankind in God’s likeness.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct, with no prefix or suffix. The initial ב is the first root consonant.

analysis.evidence: In בְּיוֹם בְּרֹא אֱלֹהִים אָדָם, אֱלֹהִים is the subject of בְּרֹא, “to create,” and אָדָם is its object. The verse then refers to the same creator with the masculine singular verb עָשָׂה, “he made.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular reference. No prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In בְּיוֹם בְּרֹא אֱלֹהִים אָדָם, אָדָם is the object of בְּרֹא, “when God created humankind.” The reference to making humankind in God’s likeness echoes Genesis 1:26–27. The singular אֹתוֹ agrees with the grammatically singular אָדָם.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, used collectively, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In בִּדְמוּת אֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֹתוֹ, the construct noun takes אֱלֹהִים as its complement. The phrase describes how God made the human, in the likeness of God.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition בִּ «in» + feminine singular common noun in the construct state.

analysis.evidence: In בִּדְמוּת אֱלֹהִים, “in the likeness of God,” the marked noun identifies whose likeness Adam bears. It refers to the creator named earlier in the verse, who is also the subject of the singular עָשָׂה, “he made.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular reference.

analysis.evidence: The clause בִּדְמוּת אֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֹתוֹ means “in the likeness of God he made him.” It echoes בְּרֹא אֱלֹהִים אָדָם, “when God created humankind,” which identifies God as the maker and אָדָם as the referent of אֹתוֹ.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Gen.5.1 to the existing object-pronoun sense of the particle in et.
draft.definition: With a pronominal suffix, אֵת expresses the direct object separately from the verb.
draft.evidence: In Gen.5.1, עָשָׂה אֹתוֹ means “he made him.” The suffix refers to אָדָם in the preceding clause.

analysis.evidence: בְּרֹא אֱלֹהִים אָדָם names אָדָם as the one God created. עָשָׂה אֹתוֹ then refers back to him as the one God made in his likeness.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle in its suffixed form אֹת־ with the third-person masculine singular pronominal suffix ־וֹ.
analysis.sense: Carries a suffix that expresses the direct object of a verb.
